newsitem.title: USA: Zenith plans to cut work force by 25 percent.
newsitem.headline: Zenith plans to cut work force by 25 percent.

text.p: Zenith Electronics Corp., citing "huge losses," said Wednesday it plans to cut 1,175 jobs, more than 25 percent of the consumer electronics company's work force.
Zenith President Peter Willmott said the company plans to eliminate about 375 salaried positions, reducing its U.S. salaried work force to fewer than 1,500.

The Glenview, Ill.-based company said it plans to cut about 800 hourly positions, largely through attrition, at its Melrose Park, Ill., colour picture tube plant as new automated processes improve productivity.
This will reduce Zenith's total U.S. hourly work force to about 2,000.
"Our fixed costs are simply too high for a company with sales at our levels and reporting such huge losses," Willmott said in a letter to employees.
He called the company's plans "a necessary step in Zenith's turnaround process."
The job cuts are expected to reduce expenses by about $20 million in 1997 and result in a fourth-quarter restructuring charge of about $25 million.
In October, Zenith reported net losses of $109 million for the first nine months of 1996.
The company said it is in discussions with its lenders and expects to amend certain financial covenants in its lending agreement.

Zenith's largest shareholder is LG Electronics Inc. of South Korea, known in part for its GoldStar electronics products. The Korean company, which makes semiconductors as well as automobiles, owns 55 percent of Zenith's outstanding shares.
Zenith's stock lost 87.5 cents to $11.625 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
